input.reasoning:
Team capacity: Backend 1.5 FTE (~60 hrs/week), Frontend 1.0 FTE (~40 hrs/week), QA 0.6 FTE (~24 hrs/week), DevOps 0.4 FTE (~16 hrs/week). This is a small team for a 24-item backlog spanning auth, payments, migration, i18n, accessibility, analytics and decommissioning — realistically a 6-7 month effort at this staffing level.

I estimated effort per backlog item by role based on typical complexity for each type of work (auth/payments/migration are backend+QA heavy; UI/UX items are frontend heavy; CI/observability/decommission are DevOps heavy), scaled unestimated items using analogous sized ones and item descriptions, and then aggregated into role totals. I capped total hours per role to what's plausible given headcount (assuming ~5-6 months elapsed calendar time, ~22 weeks), flagging under-staffing risk on Backend and DevOps given the amount of urgent/high work (payments, RBAC, migration, CI, observability, rate limiting) they need to cover.

Rates and roles used exactly as given. Non-labour costs are estimated for third-party services (Stripe fees are usage-based, not included, but need Stripe sandbox/dev account and other software), a data migration one-off tooling/environment cost, and a translation/QA-config buffer for staging infra.

Priority breakdown sums labour cost per item priority band based on the per-item allocation aggregated up to role costs.

Reductions: descope low-priority items (support ticket sync, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, decommission legacy immediately) to defer; reduce accessibility pass scope to core screens only in this phase; trim QA hours by tightening automated regression scope; defer multi-currency to phase 2.

Because there's no historical actuals data for this project, estimates carry meaningful uncertainty; I've reflected that via scenario percentiles (P50/P75/P90) with widening ranges.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox, PCI/compliance review support tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licenses and one-off migration environment
Staging/CI infrastructure (cloud costs) for pipeline duration
Contingency / project management buffer (10% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals/spend data exist yet for this project; estimate is built from backlog description, points where given, and analogous sizing for unestimated items — treat as a rough-order-of-magnitude estimate, not a committed budget.

Story points given are relative sizing only; unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-described items (e.g. PW-2 design system ~ sized like PW-5/PW-13; PW-8 migration sized larger due to explicit 400k/2M record volume).
Team works at standard 1 FTE = 40 hrs/week; overall calendar duration assumed ~22-24 weeks (5-6 months) to fit the backlog into the given headcount.

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the volume of Urgent/High backend-heavy work (auth, payments, RBAC, migration, CI, observability, rate limiting); this is flagged as a scheduling/capacity risk that could extend timeline rather than just cost.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to focus test effort on Urgent/High priority items (auth, payments, GDPR, 2FA) with lighter regression coverage on Low priority items.
Stripe transaction fees themselves are excluded (usage-based, billed directly to client) — only integration/sandbox effort and tooling are costed.
PW-24 (decommission legacy portal) and PW-18 (admin back-office) assumed deferred to a later phase in the base case but included at minimal scoping cost here; full descope reflected in reductions.
Contingency of 10% of labour cost included as a non-labour buffer line to account for estimation uncertainty given lack of actuals.

Priority breakdown allocates each backlog item's estimated labour cost fully to its stated priority band; items without story points were assigned an estimated effort consistent with their description for this purpose.

reductions.description: Descope PW-12 (support ticket submission), PW-18 (admin back-office), PW-19 (usage analytics), PW-23 (contract tests) and PW-24 (decommission legacy) — all Low priority — to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~5 Low-priority backlog items from this phase; reduces Backend/Frontend/QA hours proportionally.

reductions.description: Narrow PW-15 (accessibility pass) to the top 5 customer-facing screens now, deferring full WCAG 2.2 AA coverage across the whole app to phase 2.
reductions.effect: Cuts Frontend and QA hours on accessibility by roughly 60%.

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 (multi-currency support) until post-launch; ship single-currency (USD) first.
reductions.effect: Removes Backend/Frontend effort and the FX rate feed subscription line.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on Medium-priority items by tightening automated test scope and relying more on developer-owned unit tests.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~100 QA hours from Medium-priority backlog items.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate a representative subset first, defer full 2M invoice-line migration until after go-live.
reductions.effect: Reduces migration tooling cost and Backend/DevOps effort in this phase; remaining migration billed in a later phase.
